content_voiceover: Histiocytosis syndromes result from excess proliferation and accumulation of dendritic cells, monocytes, and macrophages, sometimes along with eosinophils and lymphocytes, depending on the specific subtype. The World Health Organization classification splits these into three types. Type one covers dendritic cell disorders, and this is where Langerhans cell histiocytosis, or L C H, lives, including the older names you might still see on boards, like eosinophilic granuloma for localized bone disease, Hand Schuller Christian syndrome for multisystem disease with bone involvement, diabetes insipidus, and exophthalmos, and Abt Letterer Siwe syndrome for the disseminated form with risk organ dysfunction. Also in type one are juvenile xanthogranulomatosis and Erdheim Chester disease. Type two covers macrophage related disorders, and this is the hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis family, including familial and infection associated and malignancy associated hemophagocytic syndromes, plus Rosai Dorfman disease. Type three is the malignant histiocytic disorders, like dendritic cell related or macrophage related histiocytic sarcoma, and monocytic leukemia or sarcoma. For boards, the key organizing principle is: type one is dendritic cell, type two is macrophage and hemophagocytic, type three is frankly malignant.
keypoints: Type I: dendritic cell disorders, includes LCH (formerly eosinophilic granuloma, Hand-Schuller-Christian, Letterer-Siwe)
Type II: macrophage-related disorders, includes HLH and Rosai-Dorfman disease
Type III: malignant histiocytic disorders, includes histiocytic sarcoma and monocytic leukemia
Classification driven by which immune effector cell proliferates: dendritic cell, macrophage, or malignant clone
keypoint_voiceover: Remember the three WHO types of histiocytosis. Type one is dendritic cell disorders, home of Langerhans cell histiocytosis and its old eponyms. Type two is macrophage related disorders, which includes hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis and Rosai Dorfman disease. Type three is the malignant histiocytic disorders, like histiocytic sarcoma.
